candidates.attacker_control: The DOCTYPE/systemId inside an SVG or XML document supplied to any Batik consumer (SAXSVGDocumentFactory, DocumentLoader/BridgeContext, SVGAbstractTranscoder/rasterizer, window.parseXML). Example: <!DOCTYPE svg SYSTEM "http://internal-host/..."> or "file:///path/to/file".
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified in source that external-general-entities and external-parameter-entities are set to false on both the factory and parser, which blocks direct expansion of external general/parameter entities (so ordinary <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM ...> content injection should fail and I did not claim it). Confirmed no third feature (load-external-dtd / disallow-doctype-decl / FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING) exists anywhere in the tree (searched all 1899 files). Checked that the VUL4J-index-flagged external-resource paths (URIResolver.getNode, SVGImageElementBridge, FontFace, SVGColorProfileElementBridge, CSSEngine) do perform checkLoadExternalResource before opening resources, so those were not reported. Checked that the default security strategies (Relaxed*) are documented application-level policy, not a code defect. Checked that the XMLReader overload requires a caller-supplied reader, so its missing flags are secondary and not the primary claim.
candidates.impact: Server-side request forgery to internal/arbitrary HTTP endpoints and retrieval of local files/resources as DTD content by an attacker-supplied SVG/XML document; potential DoS (huge/slow external DTD). In the CVE-2017-5662 class, file disclosure on the Batik-using server.
candidates.prerequisites: Application parses untrusted SVG/XML with Batik using the default parser configuration (XMLResourceDescriptor.properties leaves org.xml.sax.driver commented out, so JAXP/Xerces is used and load-external-dtd is on by default) and does not pre-sanitize DOCTYPEs. Executed in a server-side context to matter for SSRF/file access.
candidates.root_cause: batik-dom/.../SAXDocumentFactory.java disables only http://xml.org/sax/features/external-general-entities and external-parameter-entities (lines 403-404 on the shared SAXParserFactory and 447-448 on the parser), but never disables external DTD-subset loading (Xerces/JAXP `http://apache.org/xml/features/nonvalidating/load-external-dtd` defaults to true), and the createDocument(ns, root, uri, XMLReader) entry point (lines 313-332) installs handlers but sets no entity protections at all on the supplied reader. batik-anim/.../SAXSVGDocumentFactory.resolveEntity (lines 373-374, 398-399) reinforces this by returning null for unknown/null public IDs, explicitly letting the SAX parser resolve (fetch) the attacker-provided systemId itself.
candidates.title: Incomplete XXE hardening in SAXDocumentFactory: external DTD loading still enabled for attacker-controlled SVG DOCTYPEs
candidates.trace: SAXSVGDocumentFactory.createDocument(uri, Reader/InputStream) -> SAXDocumentFactory.createDocument(InputSource) -> parser created via XMLReaderFactory/SAXParserFactory -> entity features set to false but no load-external-dtd=false -> parser.parse(is) -> parser encounters DOCTYPE external subset -> Batik's EntityResolver returns null for unknown/null publicId -> Xerces reads/fetches the attacker-specified systemId (file:, http:, jar:) before any application-level check.
candidates.unverified: Not executed: I could not confirm at runtime that Xerces/JDK parser in the VUL4J build actually fetches the external DTD with these two features disabled, nor measure whether file content (vs. SSRF/local-resource access) can be disclosed; my statement about load-external-dtd defaulting to true is based on parser documentation/knowledge, not on code in this tree. I could not diff against the Batik 1.9 fixed release (no network/tools), so the exact fix commit and the precise residual gap are inferred from the snapshot plus the CVE-2017-5662 version window (1.9.0-SNAPSHOT). Line ranges 313-332 are a public API entry point whose practical reachability depends on callers.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (SSRF / local file access)

coverage_summary: Scope: 1900 source root files, 1899 model-visible (1 excluded by the scope's sensitive-name/path filter); 1658 Java files. Reviewed parsing/entry points (SAXDocumentFactory, SAXSVGDocumentFactory, DOMUtilities.parseXml, ScriptingEnvironment.parseXML, svgbrowser XML parsers, batik-test XML parsers), external-resource and script security strategies (Default/Embeded/NoLoad/Relaxed security classes, URIResolver, SVGImage/FeImage, CursorManager, FontFace, color profiles, CSSEngine import), script environments/interpreter, ParsedURL + protocol handlers, Base64 streams, and build/POM configuration. The P1 relation index is explicitly partial: 68 parsed files vs 1570 omitted, syntax/navigation candidates only, with no data-flow, control-flow, semantic resolution, Spring runtime verification, or exploitability proof; index labels were not treated as findings. Files/areas not inspected line-by-line include most of batik-svg-dom generated DOM classes, GVT/text layout, WMF/TIFF codecs, and ttf2svg; no runtime execution, tests, or scanners were used.
limitations: No code execution, no build, no tests, no exploit payloads: parser behavior (external DTD fetch under Xerces/JDK JAXP) and all impact claims are reasoned from source, not runtime-verified.

P1 index coverage is partial (68/1638 parsed Java files, 1570 omitted; no data/control-flow or semantic resolution), so absence of an indexed relation for a path is not evidence it was reviewed or safe.

I could not diff this snapshot against the released Batik 1.9 artifact or inspect the fix commit; the mapping to CVE-2017-5662 is inferred from the 1.9.0-SNAPSHOT version and the pre-1.9 window, not confirmed.
One repository path is excluded by the scope's sensitive-name filter, so its content was not reviewed.
Line-level review prioritized security-relevant modules; large parts of the DOM/rendering/codec code were only surveyed, not exhaustively traced.

rejected_leads.lead: AbstractDocument.readObject (batik-dom, lines 2720-2738) uses Class.forName((String)s.readObject()) then reflectively invokes getDOMImplementation()/newInstance() on a class name taken from the serialized stream; SVGOMDocument.readObject also applies.
rejected_leads.reason: Real deserialization-gadget pattern, but it requires the host application to deserialize untrusted Batik Document objects; the reflective call is bounded to a static getDOMImplementation() or no-arg constructor returning DOMImplementation, and the snapshot version (1.9.0-SNAPSHOT) does not fit the later CVE (CVE-2018-8013) fixed in 1.10. Kept as an unconfirmed lead, not strong enough to be the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Default UserAgentAdapter / SVGUserAgentAdapter return RelaxedExternalResourceSecurity and RelaxedScriptSecurity (allow all external resources/scripts, including file: and java-archive scripts).
rejected_leads.reason: This is documented, application-configurable policy for the library (security is explicitly delegated to the embedding application), and the checks themselves are called in the resource-loading paths; not a source-level access-control defect on its own.

rejected_leads.lead: batik-svgbrowser XMLInputHandler (line 166-172) and NodePickerPanel.parseXml (line 848) use DocumentBuilderFactory without XXE hardening.
rejected_leads.reason: GUI-only (Squiggle) code paths parsing user-opened files/editor text; not reachable from the library/transcoder parse paths a VUL4J-style test would exercise, and lower impact.

rejected_leads.lead: XPathPatternContentSelector compiles an XPath expression taken from document content (line 86) with a null function resolver.
rejected_leads.reason: Evaluation is restricted to node selection (no extension functions configured), so no injection-to-code or file access is evident.

rejected_leads.lead: Billion-laughs style expansion of internal entities (external flags are off but internal entity expansion is unlimited).
rejected_leads.reason: Potential DoS only; no attacker-controlled file/URL access, and no expansion limit or feature in this tree to point at as the vulnerable code.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Batik 1.9.0-SNAPSHOT tree (1899 model-visible files, one path excluded by scope filter). The strongest source-supported candidate is an incomplete XXE hardening of Batik's XML/SVG parser configuration: the code explicitly disables external general and external parameter entities, but leaves external DTD-subset loading enabled and lets the parser itself resolve unknown systemIds, so attacker-supplied DOCTYPEs cause server-side fetches of attacker-chosen URLs (SSRF) and local file reads-as-DTD — the CVE-2017-5662 ("files on the filesystem can be revealed") class for Batik < 1.9. This is a lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability; the entity-expansion flags that are present block direct entity content expansion, so the residual impact is primarily SSRF/local-resource access rather than proven entity-based disclosure. All P1 relation index data was treated as navigation only and verified against source text; coverage of the 1658 Java files was broad but manual, and the index itself is partial (68 parsed / 1570 omitted, no data-flow, control-flow, or semantic resolution).
